scope: Review round 13's fixes in 581c5f4b. The receive signal compares the term against the bus client's installed connection (ConnectedConn). The reconnect work runs on a goroutine of the client's, so a disconnect no longer waits behind the hooks. Also the four minor changes: README and changelog worst case 14.5 s, the never-installed clear removed, lease.go standDown with owesAckWait and no dead guard, and connectCallbacks.

proof.criterion: A holder whose receive connection is cut while its reconnect hooks still run (the KV rewatch hook hanging and failing) releases the lease, and a standby delivers within the 15 s hard bound (review round 13, defect 2, on real processes).
proof.surface: two real envoy-listener processes signed in as the machine's nkey user under the rendered grant, on a real nats-server. pod-a's receive connection runs through the lane relay, which drops '$JS.API.STREAM.INFO.KV_envoy_roles' requests on it. That connection is cut until pod-a notices and then healed, so nats.go reconnects in place. One second later it is cut again with every new dial held (a route that drops packets). The row checks that the hooks had not failed when the second cut landed and had failed by its end.
proof.observed: 7 of 7 PASS. pod-b took the lease 6.189-7.089 s after the second cut; in the 7-run batch the slowest message per run was 12.182, 12.448, 13.091, 12.208, 12.184, 13.055 and 12.175 s; a single run before the batch gave 12.162 s. Every message arrives once, and the messages after the second cut arrive in publish order.
